sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:60

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:60:1
items.html:
A difference between the first time, at the time of the emanation, and the time after it: For it was explained above in the words of the ARI, page 340, that at first the light expanded in Mati and Lo Mati, in ten emergences and ten entries of all ten lights, until it came to Malchut; and afterwards Mati and Lo Mati was made a second time, in a perpetual manner, that is, that every time the expansion reaches Malchut it goes round and round, study it there. And it was explained there that the first aspect — that is, the Mati and Lo Mati until it reached Malchut a single time — is what is called the Partzuf of Hochma of AK, or AB of AK; whereas the perpetual Mati and Lo Mati that goes round and round is another aspect, called the Partzuf of Bina of AK, or SAG of AK.
And this is what he says, “that there is a difference between the first time, at the time of the emanation” — that is, the Mati and Lo Mati of the first time, until it reached Malchut — “and the time after it,” that is, the Mati and Lo Mati after it reached Malchut the first time, which is the perpetual Mati and Lo Mati, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:60:2
items.html:
At the first time of all, etc., they were in two vessels, etc.. For these two vessels, of male and female, emerged at the time of the return of the light to the Partzuf, by the force of the doubled strikings of the record that remained in Keter against the light that comes anew to the Partzuf. And the ARI explained above (Part 4, Chapter 4, item 6) that although a small light does not strike a light greater than it, nevertheless, since there is a superiority in the light of Hochma, which now comes anew from above — which is not so with the record, whose coupling and light have already departed — Hochma can therefore strike the record and bring out sparks from her, study it there well. And this reason suffices only for the light of Hochma, which, because it comes anew from the coupling above, is thereby equalized with the record whose coupling has already departed. But this does not suffice for the Partzuf of Bina of AK; for the light of Bina, although it comes anew, still has no power strong enough to strike the record and bring out sparks for the need of a vessel. And therefore no vessel was made here for the female, but she clothes in the vessel of the male that remained from the preceding second expansion.
And furthermore, the whole reason for the striking of the lights one against the other, the ARI wrote above (Part 4, Chapter 3, item 10), is only between lights that are opposite one to the other and different in their nature, study it there. And the above Keter and Hochma are different in their nature, for the record of Keter withholds the illumination of GAR by the force of the posterior of the light of Keter that stands in the Rosh, as above in the Inner Light, page 325, the passage beginning “and therefore”; whereas the light of Hochma — her whole illumination is only the aspect of GAR, as written there. And since they are different in their nature they strike one against the other. But in the Partzuf of Bina, where the record is what remained of the light of Hochma of the second expansion, and the light that now comes anew is the light of Bina — and it is known that Hochma and Bina are not different in their nature; on the contrary, Aba and Ima dwell as one, as above in the words of the ARI in item 39 — therefore no striking applies between the record and the light of Bina, and there are here no sparks for new vessels for the need of the female. And therefore the female clothes in the vessel of the male.
And this does not contradict what the ARI wrote above in item 50, page 347, that the light of Hochma clothed in the inferior light of the record of Keter, and the light of the record of Keter inside Hochma, study it there — which shows that the light of Hochma and the record have only a single vessel, whereas here he says that they have two vessels. And the matter is that they clothe one in the other, in the likeness of the particular degrees that are in the Partzufim of Atzilut: that is, that the vessel of Hochma clothes in the vessel of Keter, and inside the vessel of Hochma clothes the coarse light of the record, and inside the coarse light of the record clothes the light of Hochma, and the choice light of the record clothes inside the light of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:60:3
items.html:
In the second departure, when the ZON rose, etc., both of them enter the vessel of the male: Namely the departure of the Mati and Lo Mati of the first time, which is called the second departure; for the Partzuf of Keter of AK is the first expansion, and the departure of the Partzuf of Keter is called the first departure, and the Partzuf of Hochma of AK is the second expansion, and the departure of the Partzuf of Hochma is called the second departure.
And just as, in the first departure, the ARI explained above, page 294, item 6, that before the second expansion the ZON of Keter rose upward — they being the record of phase four of clothing and the record of phase three — and both of them received there an illumination from the upper Keter, study it there well, so it is also in the second departure, before the expansion of the Partzuf of Bina: that the two records rose, which are the record of phase three of clothing and the record of phase two, who are the aspect of the ZON of Keter of the Partzuf of Bina. And both of them rose to the Malchut of the Rosh, and there they received together an illumination from the upper Keter; and through this illumination the female attained equivalence with the male, and therefore the female was able to clothe in the vessel of the male.
